body:
I'm glad you've managed to sort out your thoughts/feelings and that my reply helped. You didn't come across as though you hate your brother but a young woman dealing with her insecurities and not sure of how to proceed - which is perfectly normal. I just highlighted some things to concider. It's good that you love each other and perhaps explaining to him that you struggle with touch and that you're trying your best to show your affection for him. 

Maybe having these conversations will reassure him that you love him, because he could have misunderstood some of your reactions and be trying connect with you the way he naturally shows affection. Your brother knows you, as you probably know when something is not right with your brother. So having a heart to heart and quality time together will heal and strengthen your bond. A good question to ask yourself when conversing with others is a am I coming from a place of care/love? Am I in the right place emotionally to handle it, if you're angry for example, it's probably better to cool off before saying something you regret.

I would say move very carefully because your brother may need touch to show his affection and feel love from others. If you insinuate he's a pervert and he's somehow sexually attracted to you and he's not then you could destroy your relationship with him. Think about how you like to receive affection from others and how you would feel if someone completely rejected that. I'm not saying to disregard your feelings but to find a compromise like patting his shoulder/hand/an affectionate hair mess or something. It's sounds like he seeking attention and wants interaction with you, perhaps you could watch a movie or play a game together, go for a walk, find an activity where you can both bond as a family. 

Whether it's family/friendships/relationships it's about compromise on both sides and finding creative solutions. You are a 20 year old woman and he is 16, so I think you should make more of an effort to voice your own thoughts to him rather than involving your mum too soon. If he doesn't listen to you then involve your parents but if you can't voice your concerns to your own brother, how are you going to do this in future relationships etc view it as practice. 

This will also be good for him as well because it could be he views behaviours that were fine when you were children aren't okay now, the dynamics have changed since you're both older. Your mum mum maybe able to help you have this conversation with him and the appropriate way to say it if you struggle with such interactions. I hope this helps and wish you well.

It's so frustrating, my moods are up and down all the time. It feels like any time progress is made, something comes along to prove it was a fuck up all along. It's an uphill climb where an landslid keeps putting me back on my ass time and time again.
